maria: Quick flag — noticed a weird jump in per-model unit cost on the cost dashboard after yesterday's routing policy tweak. :eyes:
kevin: which model? can you paste the query or screenshot?
maria: looks like m-small-v2 but only for requests that hit the prefetch path. Sample: `SELECT model, path, sum(tokens)*unit_cost as cost FROM token_events WHERE ts > now() - interval '1 day' GROUP BY model,path` -> prefetch shows ~3x cost vs baseline
olga: hmm, did we change quantization profiles or fallback chain?
sam: no quant changes. we did add a routing rule to prefer prefetch for low-latency tenants (canary). maybe cache credits not being applied for those invocations.
maria: that's my hunch. console shows cache_savings column 0 for many prefetch hits. screenshot: https://img.redwood/costs/alerts/abc
kevin: @sam can you check router logs for the canary cohort? specifically headers: `x-redwood-route: prefetch` and `x-cache-credit`
sam: pulling logs. quick note: rollout lasted ~45m yesterday and targeted ~15% of traffic for a set of tenants.
console-bot: deploy-greenbird-2026-04-02 finished (ci 7890) by @ci-bot :white_check_mark:
maria: ok if credits missing it's an attribution bug not a real cost spike. but UX on the dashboard is confusing — when credits are zero we show full cost which freaks product teams out.
olga: agree. proposal: add a column "post-credit unit cost" and a tiny info tooltip that shows how credits were applied. also add an alert rule when prefetch path cost delta > 50% over baseline for > 10m.
kevin: +1. For the backend, add a reconciliation job that backfills cache credits for 24h window and emits an audit event. SQL-ish sketch: ```-- backfill cache credits insert into econ_adjustments (invocation_id, credit, reason) select i.id, c.estimated_credit, 'prefetch-backfill' from invocations i join prefetch_audit c on i.id = c.invocation_id where i.ts > now() - interval '1 day' and not exists (select 1 from econ_adjustments e where e.invocation_id = i.id);```
sam: i'll check whether prefetch_audit exists for the canary cohort. if not, router might have missed tagging invocations.
maria: from a rollout perspective, can we pause the canary until we confirm crediting? i'd rather reduce noise to SRE oncall.
kevin: pausing now. @releasebot can you hold canary greenbird?
console-bot: action queued: pause-rollout greenbird (reason: econ investigation)
maria: thanks. i'll open a quick dashboard PR with post-credit column and a banner showing the affected timeframe. will ping for UX review.
olga: and let's add a regression test in the econ pipeline that simulates prefetch tokens and expects credits != 0.
kevin: great next steps. file a short postmortem if the backfill runs and affects billing numbers.
maria: will do. thx team :raised_hands:
